component_postures.basis: USDA Grain Transportation Report documented VLSFO near $960/metric ton on March 11, up 79% in two weeks, and IFO 380 reaching an all-time high March 9.
USDA documented higher U.S. Gulf-to-Japan and Pacific Northwest-to-Japan grain ocean freight rates during the same shock interval.
BLS March PPI documented a 42.0% monthly increase in No. 2 diesel fuel within processed intermediate demand; April added a further 12.6% monthly increase.

BLS recorded March transportation/warehousing price pressure and an April acceleration, including 5.0% final-demand transportation/warehousing and 8.1% truck-freight price increases, while USDA separately documented materially higher rail fuel surcharges tied to diesel conditions.

BLS March CPI recorded motor fuel +21.5% month over month seasonally adjusted and gasoline +21.2%, with gasoline +18.9% year over year. This is the clearest immediate consumer-price burden visible in the national March lanes.
component_postures.causal_limit: Temporal alignment with the broader energy shock does not isolate shipping fuel or diesel as sole cause.

component_postures.basis: Nationwide CPI food was flat month over month in March, then food at home rose 0.7% in April. The March nationwide food-at-home index remained 1.9% above its year-earlier level despite a -0.2% seasonally adjusted monthly move, so no affordability improvement is inferred.

National retail scanner evidence shows February 2026 food-and-beverage dollar sales rose 1.4% year over year while unit sales fell 0.6%; in March dollar sales rose 1.7% while unit sales were only 0.1% higher, effectively flat unit purchasing despite higher spending. April unit sales then fell 4.0% while dollar sales fell only 1.7%, though calendar effects complicate that month.

Higher or persistent food price levels combined with dollar spending growth and flat/falling unit purchases are consistent with constrained real food acquisition at the national retail aggregate level. This does not establish the experience of every household or state and does not measure weight, calories, nutrition quality, or wages directly.

The March-April cross-category map shows the earliest clear consumer-price signal in motor fuel, the earliest clear upstream distribution signal in diesel and transportation costs, and later visible national food-price acceleration in April. Food real-acquisition pressure was already present before/during March, so aggregate year-over-year unit data cannot cleanly date it as a new post-shock effect. Utility cost pressure was also present but is not established as the first March-shock manifestation.

Under the frozen nationwide CPI-U monthly consumer-category comparator and primary March 9-11 marine-fuel-shock clock, food was not uniquely the first category to show monthly movement. This is a narrow ordering result only; it does not address quantity compression, substitution, shrinkflation, or household purchasing power.
Current preserved first-party text does not authorize an exclusivity claim, and observed food prices, energy costs, and purchasing behavior have multiple contemporaneous causal inputs.

affordability_guard: Underlying essential need, monthly CPI, year-over-year CPI, dollars spent, units purchased, physical weight/volume, calories/nutrition, package size, contracted commodity rate, delivered total utility cost, wages/income, geography, and household basket composition are distinct state variables. No one of them may be used as a substitute for another without explicit evidence.
component_resolution_rule: Supported intermediate transition links and quantity/affordability pressure may receive component support without converting the terminal forecast into RESOLVED_CORRECT; a failed terminal ordering component likewise does not erase supported mechanism or real-economy effects.
overall_interpretive_shift: The March 18 lane now shows a more complete essential-burden sequence than the monthly CPI ordering test alone conveyed: diesel and distribution costs spiked, motor fuel was the clearest immediate national consumer-price burden, food affordability was already strained in real-acquisition terms, and national food-price acceleration became visible in April. The broader shipping/freight/diesel-to-food mechanism is therefore stronger than the V1 CPI result alone suggested, while the literal claim that food consumer prices were uniquely first remains not supported under V1.
next_gate: Preserve any retrievable March 18 transcript to determine whether the video narrows, broadens, or qualifies the subtitle-level ordering claim. Extend the essential-burden map with package-size-adjusted physical food volume, income-adjusted essential-cost burden, and local delivered-utility-cost evidence where authoritative and comparable data are available.
